Getting started with selectiveHotelling

Source: vignettes/selectiveHotelling.Rmd
selectiveHotelling.Rmd

This vignette shows the basic workflow. The tutorial in the package repository (tutorial/) covers each function in more detail.

library(selectiveHotelling)

Cluster, then test

We simulate n=60n = 60 observations from three groups and cluster them with kk-means.

set.seed(1)
X <- rbind(matrix(rnorm(40), 20, 2),
           matrix(rnorm(40), 20, 2) + 4,
           matrix(rnorm(40), 20, 2) - 4)
res <- selective_hotelling_test(X, k1 = 1, k2 = 2, K = 3, M = 1000)
res
#> Selective Hotelling T^2 test (unknown covariance)
#>   Clusters tested : 1 vs 2 (of K = 3)
#>   Sampler         : besag-clifford
#>   Conditioning    : pair-preserved
#>   Observed T^2    :  1405
#>   Selective p-val : 0.004655 (MC s.e. ~ 0.002)
table(res$cluster)
#> 
#>  1  2  3 
#> 20 20 20

res$pval is the selective p-value for the null hypothesis that the observations in clusters 1 and 2 share one mean. The default path length is M = 5000; we use M = 1000 here so that the vignette builds quickly. The covariance matrix of the features is never estimated.

The naive test is not valid

When all observations come from one group, the clusters still look different, and the classical Hotelling test rejects almost always. The selective test does not.

set.seed(2)
X0 <- matrix(rnorm(60 * 2), 60, 2)
res0 <- selective_hotelling_test(X0, k1 = 1, k2 = 2, K = 3, M = 1000)
cl <- res0$cluster
n1 <- sum(cl == 1); n2 <- sum(cl == 2); p <- 2
F_stat <- (n1 + n2 - p - 1) / ((n1 + n2 - 2) * p) * hotelling_T2(X0, cl, 1, 2)
c(naive = pf(F_stat, p, n1 + n2 - p - 1, lower.tail = FALSE), selective = res0$pval)
#>        naive    selective 
#> 6.786752e-13 4.538853e-03

Other clustering algorithms 

selective_hotelling_test(X, k1 = 1, k2 = 2, K = 3, clustering = "hclust", M = 1000)$pval
#> [1] 0.00832417

cl_fun <- function(x) cutree(hclust(dist(x), method = "complete"), k = 3)
selective_hotelling_bc(X, cl_fun, k1 = 1, k2 = 2, M = 1000)$pval
#> [1] 0.0006205319

Any function that maps a data matrix to cluster labels can be used as cl_fun, as long as it gives the same labels every time it is run on the same data.
